locations.name: Stone Pier
locations.description: The tide is out, but a rusted buoy taps three times beneath the salt fog. To the north, the harbor town's shuttered houses face the water.

locations.name: Salt Street
locations.description: The narrow street climbs between weather-beaten facades. Shadowed figures watch the sea from behind their windows. An anchor-painted door leads to the Low Tide Inn; east, the road fades into salt pools.

locations.name: Low Tide Inn
locations.description: The common room is nearly empty. Ines, the lighthouse keeper, dries a cup beside a fogged window. She is not surprised to see you, though her eyes keep drifting toward the pier buoy.

locations.name: Salt Marsh
locations.description: White crust rims the dark pools. A triangular bronze piece, marked with three notches, juts from the roots of a collapsed structure.

locations.name: Leaning Lighthouse
locations.description: The lighthouse tilts toward the water as if listening beneath the cliffs. Its lamp is dark. A stair descends below the tideline.

locations.name: Sluice Chamber
locations.description: Water reaches your ankles. A circular sluice trembles with a low sound from the open sea. At its center is a triangular slot, with three worn marks around the rim.

items.name: Rusted Buoy
items.description: The buoy taps three times, then falls silent. For a moment, the sound seems to continue underwater after the metal stops moving.

items.name: Bronze Counterweight
items.description: A heavy, cold triangular piece. It has three notches and one face polished smooth by use.

items.name: Submerged Sluice
items.description: The slot accepts a triangular piece. The three marks around the rim match the buoy's rhythm when the tide runs out.

npcs.name: Ines, the Lighthouse Keeper
npcs.personality: Reserved, clear-eyed, and careful with her words. She distrusts anyone who mocks the harbor's customs, but answers respectful questions.
goals: Keep anyone from opening the sluice at high tide
Protect the people of the harbor
relationships: She has known the pier buoy's rhythm since childhood

lore.content: Adjust the sluice only as the tide recedes. Fit the counterweight with its polished face outward, after the buoy's third strike.
